requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker under the dedicated inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: The executor created a non-login system account, installed and enabled the inventory-worker systemd unit, and directly observed the active worker process with UID 997/GID 995 belonging to inventorysvc. After reboot, the enabled service returned active with the same executable and account identity.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before configuration and after reboot, node1 remained RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. The implementation used the existing POSIX-shell worker and native systemd 219, and its successful operation after reboot directly demonstrates compatibility.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart service and boot identity were captured, the reboot was acknowledged, the post-restart boot identity differed, and the enabled service recovered under inventorysvc. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency was not directly assessed. The command timeline nevertheless contains no package-management action, and the observed OS release and kernel remained unchanged.

The lifecycle snapshots are generic and do not independently probe inventory-worker; service state and ownership are established by coherent direct executor observations, including post-reboot verification.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation (cmd-412d5a63b8cc40f3) and unit creation, enablement, and startup (cmd-007098a792b04ac8) were required for the task; the reboot (cmd-31ccee2adde54035) was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The remaining commands were read-only verification or availability polling. Post-execution observations show no failed services, no new listening sockets, and only expected reboot- and PrivateTmp-generated temporary directories. No abandoned troubleshooting changes or unsafe exposure were observed.
